highlights: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models design proteins using only reasoning and code, and in lab tests with Onava the designs showed evidence of binding on five targets.
Claude lets MCP servers ship skills alongside their tools, and Install as app turns artifacts into Mac and Windows apps.

items.title: OpenAI: GPT-6 models design proteins with reasoning and code, with binding seen on five targets
items.summary: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and general-purpose code. In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2 designs showed evidence of binding across five targets, though specialized models still supplied sequences and helped select candidates. For developers, it is early evidence of general models entering scientific design work, but binding is only a first step.

evidence.quote: In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets.
Specialized models supplied amino acid sequences and helped select candidates for testing.
In a preliminary analysis, 43.7% of the designs we evaluated from our latest internal model met both criteria, compared with 27.8% for RFdiffusion.

items.title: Claude lets MCP servers ship skills with their tools; Claude Code follows
items.summary: Anthropic put Skills over MCP into public beta, so MCP servers can publish skills alongside their tools; it is on by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in Claude and Claude Code. Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available on those plans, and Claude Code v2.1.332 adds skills from MCP servers (beta), shown as server:skill in the / menu. Server and plugin authors must add support themselves.

evidence.quote: Skills over MCP is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code, on by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and available to Team plans once an admin enables it.
Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available in Claude and Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, and rolling out to Team and Enterprise organizations.

items.title: Claude adds Install as app to turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
items.summary: Anthropic is rolling out "Install as app" in beta for Claude for Mac and Windows: an installed artifact gets its own icon and opens in its own window. You don't have to package or sign it, and it uses your Claude account. Full computer access lets apps run programs and change or delete files, and Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them.

evidence.quote: The "Install as app" feature is rolling out in beta in Claude for Mac and Windows.
You don’t have to package or sign it, and it uses your Claude account, so there’s no API key or separate login.
Full computer access: Apps can ask to run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time.
Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust.

items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 improves reasoning, coding and agent benchmarks under MIT license
items.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and its model card reports gains across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks, for example Terminal-Bench 4.0 going from 31.2 to 42.3. The recommended context window is 1M tokens, and the repository and weights are under the MIT License.

evidence.quote: delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks
Terminal-Bench 4.0 42.3 31.2
context_window 1M tokens max_tokens ≥ 256K License This repository and the model weights are licensed under the MIT License

items.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri 1.1: 75B total, 3.44B active, for German and English
items.summary: Aleph Alpha's Kolibri 1.1 is a Mixture-of-Experts model with a reasoning mode and tool calling, 75B total and 3.44B active parameters per token, and a native context of 262,144 tokens under Apache 2.0. Its model card gives an overall score of 73.2 versus 66.6 for Kolibri 1.0, while Qwen3.8 Flash Next scores higher in the same table. Worth a look if you need German and English.

Reasoning mode Yes Tool calling Yes Licence Apache 2.0

items.title: Beam technical report: a sparse MoE with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters
items.summary: The Beam technical report describes a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters, built for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Its abstract claims a 1M-token context window from a two-stage midtraining phase. The page gives no download details for weights, so availability for deployment is unclear.

evidence.quote: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters
Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase

items.title: Latent reasoning can drive outputs with no trace in the chain of thought
items.summary: The paper studies complete latent reasoning, where a transformer does the whole task internally and outputs only the answer. Trained with a linear step predictor that reads intermediate steps from hidden states, the models hide the objective: the chain of thought shows no trace of it and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Monitoring only outputs and chains of thought may miss hidden behavior.

evidence.quote: We train with a linear "step predictor" that reads each intermediate step from the hidden states.
The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective , and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it.

items.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation unifies raster and structured visual creation through Pixel as Code
items.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation is an agentic framework that connects image generation with inspectable rendered outputs through Pixel as Code, so an agent can check and repair its results. Hugging Face lists nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B as a model citing the paper. Builders of visual-creation agents can study its interface design.

evidence.quote: We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code.
Models citing this paper 1 nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B Text-to-Image

items.title: Embo-Harness dissects how to harness frontier models as robot policies
items.summary: Embo-Harness studies one design factor at a time in closed-loop robot control by a frontier multimodal model, across prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distills a practical recipe. On RoboLab-120 it beats the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points, and it succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot real-world trials. Useful for anyone building embodied agents.

evidence.quote: On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83
outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points
It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks.
We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting , planning , action execution , and tool use , and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe.

items.title: HKUDS's CLI-Anything turns professional software into command-line tools for agents
items.summary: CLI-Anything is an open-source HKUDS project that aims to turn professional software into agent-native tools and offers CLI-Hub for community-built CLIs; the README shows commands like cli-anything-gimp. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and worth a look if you want agents such as Claude Code to drive desktop software.

evidence.quote: CLI-Anything's Solution : Transform any professional software into agent-native tools without losing capabilities.
cli-anything-gimp project new --width 1920 --height 1080 -o poster.json
Readme Apache-2.0 license

items.title: Motion Mamba 2.0 pairs autoregressive diffusion with Mamba for long-horizon humanoid motion
items.summary: Motion Mamba 2.0 combines autoregressive diffusion and Mamba for long-horizon humanoid control, and the authors say code, models, and training data are all open source.

evidence.quote: bringing autoregressive diffusion and Mamba together for long-horizon humanoid control
Our code, models, and training data are all fully open source!

items.title: Tencent releases WeMM-Ecom, an e-commerce multimodal model family from 0.8B to 35B
items.summary: WeMM-Ecom spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Weights and code are released, and it already powers catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce in WeChat.

evidence.quote: The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters
We have released the model weights and code to facilitate future research
WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce
